title: Reverse Bonami–Beckner inequality
statement: Let $p,q,\rho\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $q<1$, $q\le p$, $p\le1$, $0\le\rho\le1$, and $\rho^2\le(1-p)/(1-q)$. For every nonnegative real-valued function $f$ on the Boolean cube, the extended power mean of order $q$ of its noise-operator image is at least the extended power mean of order $p$ of $f$: $M_q(T_\rho f)\ge M_p(f)$.
hypotheses_covered: p, q, and ρ are real
f is a real-valued function on the Boolean cube
f is nonnegative at every cube point
replaced: Let $q\le p\le1$, $q<1$, $0\le\rho\le1$, and $\rho^2\le(1-p)/(1-q)$. Every $f:\{0,1\}^n\to[0,\infty)$ satisfies $M_q(T_\rho f)\ge M_p(f)$. For nonnegative functions $u$, the extended mean is $M_r(u)=(\E u^r)^{1/r}$ when $r>0$; the same formula applies for $r<0$ when $u$ is positive everywhere. For positive $u$, $M_0(u)=\exp(\E\log u)$; if $r\le0$ and $u$ has a zero, $M_r(u)=0$. All expectations are uniform. For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform measure.
